slides.1.title: Madeira's Estufagem Heating Process
slides.1.html:
The key to Madeira's ability to age for a century is Estufagem (the heating and oxidation process).

🌡️ Two heating methods

  • Estufagem (industrial heating): the wine is placed in stainless steel tanks and heated (legal maximum 50°C, typically 40-50°C) for at least 3 months, speeding up maderization
  • Canteiro (natural heating) ⭐: casks are stored in the upper floors of the lodge, where Atlantic sun and air heat and mature the wine naturally, a slow process (up to several decades). The method used for top Madeira

🔄 The effects of maderization

  • Heating plus oxidation stabilises the wine, which is no longer afraid of heat or oxygen
  • Water evaporates, concentrating flavours
  • Develops distinctive caramel, toasted, nutty, dried-fruit and tangy flavours
  • High acidity is a natural preservative, and together with heating and oxidation allows the wine to keep for over a century
slides.2.title: Madeira's Four Main Varieties and Styles (Dry to Sweet)
slides.2.items.0.label: Sercial (very dry)
slides.2.items.0.desc: Low residual sugar (Extra Seco / Seco). High acidity and fresh, with nutty, salty-sea minerality; ideal as an aperitif
slides.2.items.1.label: Verdelho (medium dry)
slides.2.items.1.desc: Slightly higher residual sugar. Smoky and vanilla notes with medium intensity; pairs well with seafood soup
slides.2.items.2.label: Bual (medium sweet)
slides.2.items.2.desc: Noticeably sweet. Dark in colour, with complex toffee, fig and caramel flavours; perfect with cheese
slides.2.items.3.label: Malvasia (very sweet)
slides.2.items.3.desc: The sweetest and richest. Honey, apricot and tropical fruit, with a silky texture; the most popular dessert wine
slides.3.question: In Madeira, what does the "Canteiro" process refer to?
slides.3.options.0: Artificial heating to 50°C in stainless steel tanks
slides.3.options.1: Natural sun-heated ageing in the upper floors of the lodge, the method for top Madeira
slides.3.explanation: Canteiro is the natural heating method for top Madeira. Casks are placed in the upper floors of the lodge and mature slowly, over as long as several decades, using the natural temperature and air of the Atlantic climate, giving quality far above industrial Estufagem.
